The Ecosystem
For The Hobby

Connect vendors, show runners, and collectors. Discover shows, list inventory, and navigate the hobby.

Modern (1980s–Present)

  • Mass-produced, widely available
  • Rookie cards dominate value
  • Parallels, autos & patch cards
  • Serial-numbered runs (/25, /10, /1)
  • Key sets: Prizm, Topps Chrome, Bowman

Vintage (Pre-1980)

  • Scarce — most were lost or damaged
  • Condition is everything
  • Icons: Ruth, Mantle, Robinson, Mays
  • No autos or patches — just the card
  • Key sets: T206, 1952 Topps, 1933 Goudey

Pro tip: Modern cards can spike overnight on player news. Vintage holds value because supply is fixed. Both have a place in a healthy collection.

PSA

Largest & most liquid. PSA 10 is the gold standard. Best for resale.

BGS

Sub-grades per corner/surface. BGS 9.5 ≈ PSA 10 in collector circles.

SGC

Tight grading, favorite for vintage. Clean black holders.

CGC

Growing in Pokemon & TCG. Crossed over from comics grading.

TAG

Fast turnaround, newer entrant building market trust.

When to Grade

Only if card + grading cost earns more than selling raw.

Scale: PSA 10 = 5–20× raw. PSA 9 = 2–4×. Below PSA 8 the premium shrinks fast.

GradeDescriptionPSA
MT (Mint)Perfect — sharp corners, no wear.9–10
NM+Near perfect, microscopic flaws only.8–9
NMLight surface wear, corners still sharp.7–8
EX-MTMinor corner wear, light scratches.6–7
EXNoticeable wear, some creasing.5
VGObvious wear, possible small crease.4
G (Good)Heavy wear, rounded corners.2–3
P (Poor)Damage, heavy creasing, water marks.1

Price impact: 1952 Topps Mantle PSA 1 ≈ $8,000. Same card PSA 7 has sold for $750,000+.

📦 Base Cards

High print run. Most worth face value unless a key rookie.

🌈 Parallels

Same card, different color foil. Lower serial number = rarer.

✍ Autographs

On-card autos worth more than sticker autos.

🧵 Patch / Relic

Game-worn jersey piece. Prime patches worth most.

🏆 Short Prints

Intentionally scarce. Can be 10–100× the base price.

1︎ Superfractor

Only one in the world. The hobby's holy grail.

Prizm rarity ladder: Base → Silver → Red /199 → Blue /149 → Purple /99 → Gold /10 → Black /1.

🏷 eBay — Sold Listings

Filter by Sold Items only. What buyers actually paid, not current listings.

📊 Card Ladder

Sales aggregated into 30/90/365-day charts. Spot rising or falling cards.

🔄 Alt (alt.gg)

Strong on modern cards and parallels. Good for low-volume sales.

🎯 PSA Pop Report

How many copies at each grade. 12 PSA 10s out of 500 = rare. Cross-reference with price.

📱 130 Point (130point.com)

Clean eBay sold data display. Fast floor comp tool at shows.

Show floor rule: Always check eBay sold comps before handing over cash. Know the market.

✓ DO

  • Bring a want list
  • Carry cash
  • Arrive early — best cards go first
  • Use penny sleeves
  • Negotiate respectfully
  • Walk the whole floor before buying

✗ AVOID

  • Touching cards without asking
  • Lowballing aggressively
  • Buying without checking comps
  • Only bringing a debit card
  • Skipping the back tables

RC / Rookie Card

First licensed card. Most valuable year of a player's career.

PC (Personal Collection)

"That's in my PC" = not for sale.

Raw

Ungraded card. Not in a holder.

Slab

A graded card in its plastic holder.

Pop (Population)

How many of a card exist at a specific grade. Low pop = rarer.

Centering

How evenly the image sits in the border. 55/45 fine, 70/30 is bad.

LCS

Local Card Shop. Build a relationship with yours.

OBO

Or Best Offer — price is negotiable.

Flip

Buy cheap, resell quickly for profit.

Case Hit

Rare insert, once per case of boxes.
